key_insight: ScholarCatalyst introduces a benchmark for evaluating whether AI can retrieve earlier papers that truly inspire or enable new research, not just papers that are textually similar. It turns scientists' own hindsight about what helped their projects into a scalable retrieval task.
problem_solved: Current AI retrieval systems are good at finding related papers, but they do not necessarily find the prior work that actually sparked a new idea or advanced a project. This paper addresses the lack of a benchmark for measuring that higher-level, scientist-like literature discovery skill.
method: Collects researcher annotations about which earlier papers were most influential for completed projects.
Uses an automated pipeline to scale these author annotations into a benchmark dataset.
Frames the task as retrieving papers that "inspire" new research, enabling evaluation beyond standard similarity-based search.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark helps measure whether retrieval systems support real scientific discovery rather than just keyword matching. It can guide better literature search tools for researchers, ideation assistants, and discovery-oriented AI agents.

paper_title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
paper_authors: Sohyeon Kim, Yoonho Lee, Bo Liu, Dayoon Ko, Rulin Shao
